name: Clear Board
statusNote: Live and canonical — the unified trainer; feature parity across all five V1 stations, deployment gated on a CI verification harness.
oneLiner: A free, unified CROR conductor-qualification trainer — rules, signals, switching, securement, and radio calls in one app, one profile, one mastery model.
stack: Tauri v2 desktop build (NSIS installer + self-contained exe)
Plain JSON content in public/data, fetched at runtime
Node verification harness run in CI

components.name: App shell + AppContext
components.desc: HashRouter routes to the stations; a single provider owns content, profile, and settings state.

components.name: src/core
components.desc: Content loading and profile persistence, an SM-2-lite spaced-repetition model, severity classification, and a verbatim-preserved SVG signal renderer.

components.name: Reference station
components.desc: Plain-language lookup with verbatim rulebook text one tap deeper and a visible trust badge.

components.name: Drill station
components.desc: Spaced-repetition question sessions built only from verified, answerable items.

components.name: Signals station
components.desc: Signal-aspect training on the preserved renderer and encoded aspect data.

components.name: Yard station
components.desc: The switch-list switching sim — seven engine modules absorbed byte-for-byte, wrapped as a React 'imperative island'.

components.name: Radio station
components.desc: A guided 14-step radio-call walkthrough with SME-locked wording.

components.name: Verification tools
components.desc: Node harnesses (solver, content check, SR golden vectors) that gate every deploy.

dataFlow: Drill builds a session filtered to verified, answerable items, tier-aware seeded.
Each answer is graded through the SM-2-lite model; mastery is recomputed and persisted to localStorage.
Yard lazy-loads the switching engine; every move is prechecked by the rules model before it animates.
A yard win maps its rule items into the same mastery profile Drill writes.
Radio walks 14 locked steps and marks completion on the profile.
A Drill miss or Yard refusal deep-links into Reference at the exact item.
integrations: Content migrated from four predecessor tools: training-assistant (reference entries), CN Conductor Trainer (rule bank, radio steps, signal renderer), cror-signals (aspect encodings), switch-list (yard engine, puzzles, solver)
decisions: A structural firewall against ever teaching a wrong rule as correct — only verified content is gradable, enforced by filters plus a CI content-check gate.
Honest trust migration: unverified content came in as needs-review, reference-only, never graded.
The switch-list engine was absorbed byte-for-byte and wrapped, not rewritten; its solver runs as a real CI gate.
Yard wins feed the same mastery model as Drill — one profile, not per-station scores.
Correct answers only advance the schedule when actually due, so marathon sessions can't fake mastery.
No exam station ships until a subject-matter expert sets the bar — 'test-ready' is deliberately deferred.
